title: Menards Driveway Sealer: Which Pail to Buy for a Midwest Winter
metaDescription: The Menards driveway sealer to buy for most blacktop is a polymer filler sealer like Latex-ite Airport Grade; 4 to 5 pails seal a 600 sq ft drive in 2 coats.
h1: Menards Driveway Sealer: Which One Should You Buy?
keywords: best sealant for concrete driveway at menards
penetrating concrete sealer for driveway menards
intro:
The Menards driveway sealer most blacktop owners should buy is a polymer-modified filler sealer such as Latex-ite Airport Grade, with Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 as the step up for rough, neglected asphalt. A typical 600 square foot, two-car driveway takes about four or five pails for two coats. Concrete driveways need a different aisle entirely: a clear or penetrating concrete sealer, never black asphalt sealer.

Menards serves the Midwest and Great Plains, where driveways face deep frost, road salt and coal tar rules. That shifts the shopping list toward flexible, coal-tar-free products and toward crack repair before sealing. This guide does not list prices or promise what a given store has on the shelf, because both change by location and season. It tells you which kind of pail to look for, how many to buy, what else goes in the cart, and how to make the coat last through winter.
quickAnswer: For sound asphalt that has started to fade, look for a polymer-modified filler sealer such as Latex-ite Airport Grade. For rough, open asphalt that has gone years without a coat, a heavier premium pail such as Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000. For a fair driveway on a two-year cycle, a value filler sealer such as Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop. Buy a rope or pourable crack filler too. For concrete, buy a clear waterproofing sealer such as Seal-Krete Original or a penetrating silane-siloxane. Check menards.com for what your store carries.

sections.heading: Menards Driveway Sealer: The Short Answer
sections.body:
| Your driveway | What to look for | Example product |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sound blacktop, starting to gray | Polymer-modified filler sealer | Latex-ite Airport Grade |
| Rough, porous blacktop, long unsealed | Premium heavy-solids emulsion | Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 |
| Fair blacktop, sealed every 2 years | Value filler sealer | Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop |
| Cracks 1/8 to 1/2 inch wide | Rope or pourable crack filler | Latex-ite Pli-Stix |
| Plain concrete | Clear waterproofing or penetrating sealer | Seal-Krete Original, or a silane-siloxane |

The product type matters more than the brand. On asphalt, a filler sealer with polymer gives the best balance of film, flexibility and cost for Midwest winters. On concrete, a sealer that keeps salty water out of the pores is the goal.

Stock varies by store and season, and these brands are not guaranteed at every location. Use the product types in the table to choose, then check menards.com for your store before you drive over.

sections.heading: Which Driveway Sealer Should You Buy at Menards?
sections.body:
These are widely sold brands that fit Midwest conditions, chosen from manufacturer labels and data sheets, the job each formula is built for, coverage and cure requirements, and patterns in owner feedback. If your store carries a different brand, match it by type using the label vocabulary later in this guide.

### Best overall for asphalt: Latex-ite Airport Grade

A polymer-modified filler sealer from Dalton Enterprises. The polymer lets the dried coat stretch as pavement shrinks in January and swells in July, and the mineral filler closes the hairline checking that lets water in to freeze. The label lists resistance to gasoline and oil, handy on an apron where cars and snowblowers drip. Coverage is moderate, so measure carefully and plan two coats. Our full [Latex-ite review](/latex-ite-driveway-sealer-review/) covers it in depth.

### Best for rough, neglected asphalt: Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000

The top of Gardner-Gibson's Black Jack line, with heavy solids and polymer. Salt-country asphalt that has gone several winters without a coat opens up into a rough gray texture that drinks thin sealers. A heavier film fills that texture and stretches the time to the next coat, which matters when the sealing season is short. It costs more per pail, covers less on rough asphalt and is harder to pull.

### Best value for a regular reseal: Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop Filler and Sealer

An asphalt filler sealer, despite sharing a name with Rust-Oleum's garage floor epoxy. It carries enough filler for moderately weathered texture and gives a clean black. Expect to recoat on a roughly two-year rhythm where salt and plowing are part of winter. If you already reseal that often, the savings add up.

### Best prep companion: Latex-ite Pli-Stix rope crack filler

A rubberized rope you press into the crack and melt with a propane torch. In the Midwest, crack repair decides whether a sealer lasts, because water in open cracks freezes and widens them every winter. Pli-Stix suits cracks of roughly 1/8 to 1/2 inch.

### Best for concrete driveways: Seal-Krete Original

A clear, water-based waterproofing sealer for concrete and masonry. It helps the slab shed water, which is what stops freeze-thaw scaling. Where salt use is heavy, a dedicated silane-siloxane penetrating sealer gives stronger protection against chlorides. Our [concrete driveway sealer rankings](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/) compare both kinds.

sections.heading: Why Does a Midwest Driveway Need a Different Sealer?
sections.body:
Menards operates across the upper Midwest and Great Plains, and that climate shapes the right product more than the store does.

### Freeze-thaw

Water seeps into small surface cracks, freezes, expands by roughly nine percent and pries the pavement apart a little more each cycle. A Midwest winter brings dozens of those cycles. A sealer that keeps water out of the top layer slows the damage. A brittle sealer that cracks with the pavement in January lets it continue. That is why polymer-modified products tend to be worth the extra money in the northern states.

### Salt

On asphalt, deicing salt is not especially harsh on the binder, but the extra melting and refreezing it causes near the surface adds freeze-thaw cycles. On concrete, salt is a direct threat that drives scaling and spalling, especially on slabs less than a year or two old. Our guide to the [best ice melt for concrete](/best-ice-melt-for-concrete/) lists gentler options.

### Plows and shovels

Steel blades and snowblower scraper bars shave the top off any coating, especially at edges and high spots. Expect wear there first, and expect to touch up the apron and the plow path more often than the rest of the driveway.

### The short season

In much of the region, the realistic sealing window runs from late May to mid-September. A product that stretches the time between coats saves you from chasing that window every year.

sections.heading: Is Coal Tar Sealer Allowed Where Menards Operates?
sections.body:
Refined coal tar sealers were once the default in the Midwest because they resist fuel and wear well. They are also rich in polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, a group that includes several probable carcinogens. U.S. Geological Survey research linked coal-tar-sealed pavement to raised PAH levels in nearby house dust and stream sediment, and regulators responded.

### What the rules say

Minnesota banned the sale and use of coal tar sealants statewide in 2014. Several local governments elsewhere in the region, with Dane County, Wisconsin, among the early ones, adopted their own limits. Rules vary town by town, so check with your city or county if you are outside Minnesota.

### The safe default

Buy an asphalt-based, coal-tar-free sealer. Modern polymer-modified asphalt emulsions close most of the performance gap, and they are far easier on kids, pets, soil and the storm drains your driveway runoff reaches. If the pail does not say clearly, read the safety data sheet.

### Where the risk is

The main-brand pails sold in restricted areas should already comply. The risk comes from contractor-grade product bought elsewhere and from bulk sealcoat a crew brings. If you hire someone, ask in writing what product they use.

sections.heading: How Many Pails of Driveway Sealer Do You Need?
sections.body:
Measure length times width for each paved area and add them. Divide by the single-coat coverage on the pail, then double for two coats. Most filler sealers in 4.75-gallon pails list somewhere around 250 to 400 square feet per coat; heavy premium pails sit at the low end and thin sealcoats at the high end.

| Driveway | Area | Mid-range filler, 2 coats | Premium heavy pail, 2 coats |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One car, short | about 300 sq ft | 2 to 3 pails | 3 pails |
| Two car, typical | about 600 sq ft | 4 to 5 pails | 5 to 6 pails |
| Two car, long | about 1,000 sq ft | 6 to 8 pails | 8 to 9 pails |
| Rural or turnaround | 1,500 sq ft and up | 9 to 12 pails | 11 to 14 pails |

### Lean high in the Midwest

Freeze-thaw wear leaves Midwest asphalt more porous than the label average, so plan toward the higher count. Add one spare pail and keep it sealed. An unopened pail is easy to return; a store run with half the driveway wet is not.

### Plan for weight

A full pail weighs somewhere around 50 to 60 pounds, so a six-pail order is a real load for a small SUV. Use a flatbed cart and check your vehicle's payload.

### Price questions

Pail prices change by store, season and promotion, so this guide does not quote them. Check menards.com for current pricing, and see [how much it costs to seal a driveway](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/) for a full materials-and-labor comparison.

sections.heading: What Is the Best Sealer for a Concrete Driveway at Menards?
sections.body:
A concrete driveway needs a concrete sealer, not a black pail. Asphalt sealer will not bond to concrete and peels in sheets. In the concrete aisle, you choose between two kinds.

### Penetrating sealers

Silane and siloxane sealers soak in and make the pores water-repellent, with no visible film. In salt country, they are the strongest defense against scaling, because they keep salty meltwater out without leaving a film for plows and tires to wear off. Our guide to [silane vs siloxane sealers](/silane-vs-siloxane-sealers/) explains the two chemistries.

### Clear waterproofing and acrylic sealers

Clear water-based waterproofers such as Seal-Krete Original are a practical, easy-to-find middle ground. Acrylic film-formers add sheen and are the usual choice for stamped or colored concrete, but they wear in tire paths and need recoating every few years.

### Timing on new concrete

New slabs should cure for the period the sealer label lists, commonly about 28 days, and should be sealed before their first winter if possible. A first-winter slab exposed to salt with no protection is the most likely to scale.

### Deicers to avoid

Skip deicers based on ammonium nitrate or ammonium sulfate on any concrete; they attack it chemically. For a full walkthrough, see [how to seal a concrete driveway](/how-to-seal-a-concrete-driveway/) and the broader [best concrete sealer](/best-concrete-sealer/) guide.

sections.heading: What Crack Filler and Driveway Patch Should You Buy at Menards?
sections.body:
Buy repair products on the same trip as the sealer. In freeze-thaw country, unfilled cracks are the main reason a fresh coat fails.

### Match the product to the crack

| Damage | Product type |
| --- | --- |
| Hairline checking under 1/8 inch | The filler sealer itself, in two coats |
| Cracks 1/8 to 1/2 inch | Rope filler (melted in) or pourable rubberized filler |
| Cracks wider than 1/2 inch | Backer rod or sand, then filler; or a trowel patch |
| Shallow holes and broken edges | Cold patch asphalt, tamped in layers |
| Web of connected cracks | A base problem; get a paving quote |

### Rope versus pourable

Rope filler melted with a torch sets into a flexible, rubbery seal that handles freeze-thaw well, but it is slow and needs fire safety. Pourable jugs are faster for many narrow cracks but tend to shrink and need a second pass. Our [driveway crack filler rankings](/best-driveway-crack-filler/) compare specific products.

### Patching holes

Cold patch asphalt fills potholes and broken edges. Clean out loose material, fill in layers, and tamp each layer hard. Let patches and fillers cure for the time on their labels, often a day or more, before sealing over them.

sections.heading: What Else Goes in the Cart for Sealing Day?
sections.body:
### Prep

- Stiff push broom and a leaf blower or shop vac.
- Driveway cleaner or degreaser; our [driveway cleaner](/best-driveway-cleaner/) guide compares options.
- Oil-spot primer for stains that stay tacky after scrubbing. Our guide to [removing oil stains from a driveway](/how-to-remove-oil-stains-from-driveway/) covers the cleaning.
- Crack filler sized to your cracks and cold patch for holes.

### Application

- A squeegee or sealer brush on a long handle.
- A trim brush for edges.
- A drill-mounted mixing paddle; filler sealers settle hard in the pail.
- Painter's tape or plastic for the garage threshold and walks.
- Gloves, old shoes and clothes you can throw away. Dried asphalt sealer does not wash out.

### Washing

If the driveway needs pressure washing, a surface cleaner attachment avoids the stripes a wand leaves; see our [surface cleaner](/best-surface-cleaner-for-pressure-washer/) guide. Then give the driveway at least a full sunny day to dry before you seal. Trapped moisture is one of the most common causes of peeling.

### Moss and weeds

Pull weeds out of cracks and clear moss before filling; our page on [removing moss from an asphalt driveway](/how-to-remove-moss-from-asphalt-driveway/) explains how.

sections.heading: When Should You Buy and Apply Sealer in the Midwest?
sections.body:
Emulsion sealers need air and pavement at about 50 degrees F and rising, mild overnight lows and a dry day or two. In much of the Menards footprint that means late May to mid-September.

### Buy close to sealing day

An emulsion that freezes separates and is ruined. Sealer bought on late-season clearance and left in an unheated garage over winter is a common loss. Buy in the season you will use it, close to the weekend you plan to seal, and store pails indoors.

### Skip the first warm spring weekend

A 65-degree April afternoon often comes with nights near freezing, and sealer cannot cure in that cold. Wait until nighttime lows stay mild.

### Watch humidity, not just heat

Midwest summer humidity slows evaporation, which is how emulsions cure. On a sticky 85-degree day a coat can feel dry on top and still be soft underneath at sunset. Give it extra time before driving on it.

### Avoid the hottest afternoons

In July and August, sealer can flash dry before it levels and leave streaks. Mornings and late afternoons work better. Our guides on the [best time to seal a driveway](/best-time-to-seal-driveway/), [what temperature to seal a driveway](/what-temperature-to-seal-driveway/) and [how long driveway sealer takes to dry](/how-long-for-driveway-sealer-to-dry/) have the detail.

sections.heading: Should You Seal It Yourself or Hire a Sealcoating Crew?
sections.body:
Every spring, sealcoating crews leave door hangers across Midwest neighborhoods. Whether the pails are worth the effort depends on the size of the driveway.

### Short driveways favor DIY

On a one-car or typical two-car driveway, a few pails, a squeegee and a Saturday usually cost far less than a crew's minimum charge.

### Long driveways tighten the math

Crews spray commercial emulsion from bulk tanks, often with sand and polymer added on site, and their price per square foot drops as the area grows. Once you are looking at twelve or more pails plus two days of hauling and spreading, a quote from a reputable crew may land close to your material cost. Our guide to [driveway sealing costs](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/) shows what contractors commonly quote.

### Vet any crew

- Ask what product they use, in writing, and confirm it is coal-tar-free.
- Ask whether crack filling and oil-spot priming are included.
- Ask how many coats they apply.
- Be wary of door-to-door offers of leftover material from a nearby job; that pitch often means a thin, watered-down coat.

### A middle path

Fill cracks yourself every spring, when they are small and cheap to fix, and decide each cycle whether to do the topcoat yourself. For step-by-step technique, see [how to seal a driveway](/how-to-seal-a-driveway/), and compare the shelf at the other big-box chain in our [Home Depot driveway sealer](/driveway-sealer-home-depot/) guide.

sections.heading: How Do You Make a Sealer Job Last Through Winter?
sections.body:
A good coat can still be cut short by rough winter care.

### Snow removal

Set the snowblower's skid shoes so the scraper bar rides slightly above the surface. Use a plastic-edged shovel, and if you hire plowing, ask for a poly or rubber cutting edge or for the blade to be lifted slightly on sealed asphalt.

### Deicer

Use it sparingly and sweep up the excess once the ice is gone. The goal is to break the bond between ice and pavement, not to bury the driveway. Less salt means fewer melt-refreeze cycles at the surface.

### Spring check

Walk the driveway in spring and note wear in the tire paths, the plow line and the apron. Spot-treat those areas if the rest still sheds water. Fill new cracks before they widen. Our guide on [how often to seal your driveway](/how-often-should-you-seal-your-driveway/) explains how to read the wear, and our [asphalt driveway sealer rankings](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/) cover brands beyond the Menards aisle.

mistakes.title: Sealing over frost-opened cracks
mistakes.body: Every Midwest winter widens cracks, and sealer cannot bridge much more than a hairline. Coating over open cracks buys a few weeks of good looks before they reappear and water keeps freezing in the base. Fill cracks first with a flexible filler and let it cure before you seal.

mistakes.title: Buying in fall and storing pails in the garage
mistakes.body: Sealer bought on late-season clearance and left in an unheated garage can freeze over winter. A frozen emulsion separates and cannot be saved. Buy close to the weekend you will seal, keep pails indoors at room temperature, and use them the same season.

mistakes.title: Grabbing black sealer for a concrete driveway
mistakes.body: Asphalt emulsion will not bond to concrete. It peels in sheets within a season and leaves a patchy black mess that is harder to remove than it was to apply. Confirm your surface first and buy a clear waterproofing or penetrating concrete sealer for concrete.

mistakes.title: Ignoring coal tar rules
mistakes.body: Contractor or out-of-area products may still contain refined coal tar, which is banned in Minnesota and restricted in a number of towns. Using it can bring fines and leaves high-PAH dust around your home. Check the safety data sheet and stay with asphalt-based sealers.

mistakes.title: Letting the plow blade ride on the surface
mistakes.body: Steel plow edges and snowblower scraper bars shave sealer off high spots and edges all winter. Raise the skid shoes, ask your plow service to lift the blade slightly, and use poly or rubber edges where you can. The coat lasts noticeably longer in the plow path.

faqs.q: What is the best driveway sealer at Menards?
faqs.a: For most asphalt driveways, a polymer-modified filler sealer such as Latex-ite Airport Grade is the balanced choice. For rough, long-unsealed blacktop, a premium heavy pail such as Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 builds more film. For a fair driveway sealed every two years, a value filler sealer saves money. Check menards.com to see which your store carries.

faqs.q: How much does driveway sealer cost at Menards?
faqs.a: Prices change by store, season and promotion, so check menards.com for current figures. What you can plan is quantity: a 600 square foot driveway takes about four or five filler-sealer pails for two coats, plus crack filler, a squeegee, a brush and a mixing paddle. Premium pails cost more each but can stretch the time between coats.

faqs.q: What is the best sealant for a concrete driveway at Menards?
faqs.a: A clear waterproofing sealer such as Seal-Krete Original suits most concrete driveways, and a penetrating silane-siloxane sealer gives stronger protection where salt use is heavy. Use an acrylic only for stamped or colored concrete where you want sheen. Never use black asphalt sealer on concrete; it peels.

faqs.q: Is coal tar sealer legal where Menards operates?
faqs.a: Minnesota banned coal tar sealants statewide in 2014, and several cities and counties in other Midwest states restrict them locally. Rules vary, so check with your city or county. Either way, asphalt-based sealers are the safer choice for families, pets and nearby streams, and polymer-modified versions perform well.

faqs.q: What asphalt crack filler should I buy at Menards?
faqs.a: Match it to the crack width. For cracks of about 1/8 to 1/2 inch, a rope filler such as Latex-ite Pli-Stix melted in with a torch gives the most durable seal, and a pourable rubberized filler is faster for many narrow cracks. Wider cracks need backer rod first or a trowel patch, and holes need cold patch.

faqs.q: How many pails of sealer do I need for a two-car driveway?
faqs.a: About four or five pails for two coats on a typical 600 square foot driveway with a mid-range filler sealer covering roughly 250 to 350 square feet per pail per coat. Heavy premium pails may need five or six. Weathered Midwest asphalt leans toward the higher count. Add one spare pail and keep it sealed for return.

faqs.q: When is the best time to seal a driveway in the Midwest?
faqs.a: Late May to mid-September, when air and pavement stay above about 50 degrees F, nights are mild and no rain is forecast for at least a day. Avoid the first warm weekend of spring, which often brings near-freezing nights, and the hottest July afternoons, when sealer can dry before it levels.

bottomLine: Shopping for driveway sealer at Menards is really shopping for a Midwest winter. On asphalt, choose a flexible, coal-tar-free filler sealer such as Latex-ite Airport Grade, step up to a heavy premium pail like Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 for neglected blacktop, and fill frost-opened cracks before you seal. On concrete, buy a clear waterproofing or penetrating sealer instead. Check your store's stock and current prices online, buy close to sealing day so nothing freezes, seal in warm, dry weather, and protect the coat from plows and salt. That routine gets more years from every pail than any label claim.
